newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat lapses into no-trade zone.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat lapses into no-trade zone.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange wheat contracts did not trade on Thursday despite a build-up of selling orders, brokers said.
Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd was a big seller of January wheat at A$162.00 a tonne, broker Phil Lindsay said.
But the market focus was on the January contract leaving the board, with about 600 contracts now being delivered, he said.
The January futures price was right in line with the physical market after a substantial price rise to A$161.50 a tonne delivered Newcastle, he said.
Attention had switched to March futures contract, which could trade higher toward A$170.00 a tonne from Thursday's settlement of A$158.00, Lindsay said.

The Australian Wheat Board's decision to hold its pool prices steady this week was also influencing the market. Earlier expectations that the current pool would be closed off may not occur for a while because of good export demand for Australian wheat, he said.
The market was expected to remain quiet for a few weeks under the influence of the holiday season, he said.
